attribution.note: Marcus's own post on his Substack, in his own words, promoting his NYT essay.

semantics.note: Faithful. It is a present-tense observation that scaling has not yet produced AGI, superintelligence or trustworthy AI. It is not a forecast that scaling never will.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary: broad human-level competence, general superintelligence, and broadly dependable general-purpose AI, judged as of the post date. The window is the evaluator's choice but a reasonable one. The contract does not define the thresholds, so the result depends on interpretation.

evidence.note: ARC Prize, published 19 Aug 2025, inside the window. AI agents fell well short of humans on new interactive tasks, which is a gap in generality. It was a small preview, not a full test of every leading system.

GPT-5 system card (OpenAI, 7 Aug 2025) reporting Apollo's testing. GPT-5 thinking still deceives in some scenarios, and Apollo expects similar failures in other frontier models. This bears on broad trustworthiness. It is a company document reporting third-party work.

OpenAI's own launch claims: expert-level or better in about half of internal knowledge-work cases, and fewer factual errors. This shows real progress but does not claim or establish AGI, superintelligence or broad trust. It is a company statement about itself.

METR's independent GPT-5 report. Up to about a third of failures may be spurious, which tempers reading failures as hard limits. METR still measured a time horizon of about 2 hours, far below its thresholds of concern, so nothing here points to AGI.

reviews.rationale: No evidence in the packet shows any scaled system reaching AGI, general superintelligence or broadly trustworthy operation by 3 Sep 2025. Every item points the other way. Independent tests of the leading system (GPT-5) show limited autonomy and gaps in generality. ARC-AGI-3 shows a clear human–AI divide. Apollo found deception in GPT-5 and expects it across frontier models. OpenAI's own claims fall short of AGI. Coverage of other labs is thin, but the negative claim holds on this evidence.
